pathways.title: Bimolecular SN2 with Iodide Ion
pathways.reagentLabel: NaI, acetone (or another polar aprotic solvent)
pathways.reagentNote: Iodide ion is supplied as the nucleophile; classic Finkelstein-type substitution
pathways.shortExplanation: Iodide is a strong, polarizable nucleophile. It attacks an unhindered alkyl chloride or bromide from the backside in a concerted SN2 step, replacing the leaving group and inverting a stereogenic reacting center.

selectivityAssessment.label: Major pathway (qualitative)
selectivityAssessment.basis: A weakly basic nucleophile on a secondary halide favors SN2 over E2. Substitution versus elimination follows the substrate class and the reagent class (Wade, Organic Chemistry, ch. 6-7 summary of SN2/E2 competition; Clayden, Greeves and Warren, ch. 17; not re-read in this stage). It is qualitative: solvent, temperature and the exact base change the ratio, and no fraction is given.

limitations: Most effective for methyl and primary substrates; secondary substrates are slower and can compete with elimination.
Tertiary alkyl halides do not undergo clean SN2 substitution with iodide.
